character_sheet: The Cephadrome is a rideable flying hammerhead shark on legs: a hammer-headed head with a hinged mouth on a three-segment neck, a body of several blocks with a tall chest keel, two three-segment legs with feet, two four-spar wing fins with a membrane, a four-spar dorsal fin with four membranes, and a three-segment tail ending in a four-spar tail fin (ModelCephadrome.createBodyLayer, ModelCephadrome.java:129-283). It is a PathfinderMob in the ambient category (Cephadrome.java:41; ModEntities.java:733-734) with 300 HP and 70 attack (createAttributes :137-141), wanders and looks about on the ground (:130-134), and on a 1-in-7 tick hunts monsters, Mothra, the Ender Dragon, untamed Leons, Gamma Metroids and Water Dragons — and players once one has hurt it below nine tenths of its health, or when in a bad mood, or after a refused mount (customServerAiStep :352-386, isSuitableTarget :401-420) — running at 1.7 with the attacking flag up and biting within six blocks plus half the target's width for 70 (doHurtTarget :309-331, x1.5 against the Kraken, a 2.5 knockback). Fed raw meat it heals to full and lets a player mount (:56-60); ridden it flies with no gravity on the client-predicted RiderFlightController (:73-84, :182) and its wings sound every 22 ticks (:164-173) — the model's activity 1 is that ridden flight. Hits are refused for 25 ticks after each one and turn it on the attacker (hurt :334-349); it heals 2 on a 1-in-100 roll (:356-358). It spawns by day above y 50 with clear air above and no other within 16 blocks (checkSpawnRules :544-555; a spawner-born one is born hostile) through the ambient_cephadrome biome modifier. Read it as a shark that walks: a flat-bodied stride on the ground, and in the air a slow wide beat of the wing fins.
size_notes: Drawn at x1.0 of the rig (CephadromeRenderer.java:20, applied :30; shadow 1.25) on a 512x256 sheet (ModelCephadrome.java:283); 2.5 x 2.25 block hitbox (ModEntities.java:733-734). The wing fins are 70-unit spars with zero-thickness membranes. The neck, tail and tail fin are chains the code positions segment by segment — key the joints, never the positions.

groups.name: gait
groups.amplitude: pi x 0.4 x the TRUE horizontal speed in blocks per tick (from xOld / zOld, not limbSwingAmount), clamped to 0.75 rad (43 deg) once past 0.5, zero below a limbSwingAmount of 0.001: every piece of a leg swings together about its rest (upper −0.58, middle 0.98, lower −0.52, foot 0), the left leg opposite the right; in ridden flight (activity 1) both legs are held tucked one radian forward and still
groups.plain: on the ground the two legs stride with the real speed, each leg a stiff piece; ridden, they tuck forward and hold
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ACTIVITY byte (Cephadrome.java:53; 1 while ridden) selects tucked-and-still over the stride
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.75 x wingspeed 0.55 = 0.4125 rad/tick: the natural period is 2 pi / 0.4125 = 15.23 ticks; the amplitude is the entity's real speed, so the reference clip's fixed limbSwingAmount does not drive it

groups.name: wing_fins
groups.amplitude: ridden flight (activity 1): pi x 0.28 = 0.88 rad (50 deg) about zero at 0.55 x 0.55 = 0.3025 rad/tick; on the ground and calm: pi x 0.028 = 0.088 rad (5 deg) about −0.85 at 0.2 x 0.55 = 0.11 rad/tick; on the ground and attacking: pi x 0.068 = 0.214 rad (12 deg) about −0.65 at 0.9 x 0.55 = 0.495 rad/tick; the right fin the negative of the left
groups.plain: the wing fins beat wide and slow in ridden flight, hang folded with a faint stir on the ground, and half-raise and quiver while attacking
groups.math: w = activity != 0 ? cos(t * 0.55 * 0.55) * pi * 0.28 : (attacking == 0 ? -0.85 + cos(t * 0.2 * 0.55) * pi * 0.028 : -0.65 + cos(t * 0.9 * 0.55) * pi * 0.068); left spars and membrane zRot = w; right = -w
groups.phase: three branches: DATA_ACTIVITY 1 (ridden), else DATA_ATTACKING clear / set
groups.omega_note: the classic phase in flight is ageInTicks x 0.55 x wingspeed 0.55 = 0.3025 rad/tick (period 20.8 ticks); calm 0.11 (57.1 ticks); attacking 0.495 (12.7 ticks)

groups.name: top_fins
groups.amplitude: |pi x 0.05| = up to 0.157 rad (9 deg), rectified, folding only one way from the rests: spar 1 and membrane 1 the full wave about −1.85 / −0.26, spar 2 and membrane 2 a half about −2.07 / −0.52, spar 3 and membrane 3 a quarter about −2.42 / −0.89, spar 4 and membrane 4 an eighth about −2.63 / −1.11
groups.plain: the dorsal fin folds and rises very slowly, the front spar most and the rear least; the wave is rectified, so it folds twice per period
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.15 x wingspeed 0.55 = 0.0825 rad/tick: the natural period is 76.2 ticks, the visible period 38.1

groups.name: tail
groups.amplitude: segment 1: pi x 0.04 = 0.126 rad (7 deg); segments 2 and 3 and the tail fin: pi x 0.1 = 0.314 rad (18 deg) at 0.76 x 0.55 = 0.418 rad/tick, an eighth of a period apart down the chain; on the ground and calm: pi x 0.03 = 0.094 rad (5 deg) at 0.22 x 0.55 = 0.121 rad/tick; each segment placed at the end of the one before, the four fin spars and three membranes riding the fin root
groups.plain: the tail sweeps side to side in a travelling wave — brisk in flight or when attacking, a slow sway at rest on the ground
groups.math: ts = (activity == 0 && attacking == 0) ? 0.22 : 0.76; amp = (activity == 0 && attacking == 0) ? 0.03 : 0.1; tail1.yRot = cos(t * ts * 0.55) * pi * 0.04; tail2.yRot = cos(t * ts * 0.55 - pi/4) * pi * amp; tail3.yRot = cos(... - pi/2) * pi * amp; tailfin1.yRot = cos(... - 3pi/4) * pi * amp; tailfin2/3/4 and tailmembrane1/2/3 = tailfin1 (positions along the chain by cos/sin x 13 / 13 / 10)
groups.phase: state-branching: the calm ground state (activity 0 and attacking 0) selects the slow, small wave
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.76 x wingspeed 0.55 = 0.418 rad/tick (period 15.0 ticks); calm on the ground 0.22 x 0.55 = 0.121 (51.9 ticks)

groups.name: mouth
groups.amplitude: attacking: pi x 0.14 = 0.44 rad (25 deg) about −0.61; not attacking: still at −0.87
groups.plain: the lower jaw works while the attacking flag is set and hangs still otherwise
groups.phase: the synced DATA_ATTACKING byte (Cephadrome.java:51, set at :377, cleared at :383) selects
groups.omega_note: the classic phase is ageInTicks x 0.5 x wingspeed 0.55 = 0.275 rad/tick: the natural period is 22.8 ticks

behaviour: On the ground the two legs stride as stiff pieces at 0.4125 rad/tick (a 15.2-tick period), the swing scaled by the entity's TRUE horizontal speed (from its last position, ModelCephadrome.java:299-300) rather than by limbSwingAmount, and clamped at 43 degrees (:301-307); ridden (DATA_ACTIVITY 1, Cephadrome.java:53) both legs tuck one radian forward and hold (:312-321).

The wing fins branch three ways (:333-343): in ridden flight they beat 50 degrees each way at 0.3025 rad/tick (a 20.8-tick beat); on the ground they hang folded at −0.85 with a 5-degree stir, and while the attacking flag is set they half-raise to −0.65 and quiver 12 degrees at 0.495 rad/tick. The right fin mirrors the left.

The dorsal fin folds on a very slow rectified wave (a 76-tick period, folding twice in it), the front spar 9 degrees and each spar behind half the last (:345-353). The tail sweeps in a travelling wave an eighth of a period per segment — 18 degrees at 0.418 rad/tick in flight or when attacking, 5 degrees at 0.121 rad/tick at rest on the ground — and the tail fin's spars and membranes ride its end (:355-389).

The neck turns toward the look in three steps (an eighth, a quarter, a half) and the head three quarters, the hammer-head lobes and the mouth riding it (:413-432); ridden, the look is replaced by a filtered turn rate clamped to ±50 degrees (:395-405). The mouth works 25 degrees at 0.275 rad/tick while attacking and hangs at −0.87 otherwise (:434-435).
The bite (doHurtTarget, Cephadrome.java:309-331) is rolled by the 1-in-7 hunt (:365-385) and the wing sound every 22 ticks while ridden is the entity's (:164-173) — neither is an animation event.

wishlist: in `fly`: the ridden beat — the code beats the wing fins 50 degrees (ModelCephadrome.java:333) but holds the body flat; bank into turns (the yaw filter at :395-405 already turns the head) and let the tail trail the turn
in `walk`: the code scales the stride by the true speed (:299-307) — keep it short and low, a shark on legs, with the tail's travelling wave (:360-370) carried through
in `aggro_idle`: the fins half-raised and quivering (:333, the attacking branch) with the mouth working (:435) — a threat display before the bite

locked_bones_note: The design's section 6 ModelCephadrome row (geckolib_migration_design.md:445): 'head [1.3,1.0] @1; body/chest [2.3,1.4] @0.5; left/right leg chains [0.5,0.9] @0.5; wing-fin roots [1.7,0.45] @0.25; tail1/tail3 [0.8,0.7] @0.25'. head, body, chest, tail1 and tail3 resolve as written. 'left/right leg chains' is not a bone name: taken as every segment of each chain — leftleg1, leftleg2, leftleg3, leftfoot and rightleg1, rightleg2, rightleg3, rightfoot (the code poses all four pieces a side, ModelCephadrome.java:314-330). 'wing-fin roots' is not a bone name: taken as the root spar a side — the port model spells the left one 'lefwingfin1' (createBodyLayer; the geo carries that spelling) and the right 'rightwingfin1'; the row says the membranes and outer spars stay visual ('make only structural fin roots damageable').
formulas: `ModelCephadrome.poseFrom` (ModelCephadrome.java:300-450; orig ModelCephadrome.java:387-554 in `render` (func_78088_a, :373-555; func_78087_a at :563-565 is a bare super call), wingspeed 0.55 from `new ModelCephadrome(0.55f)` in orig ClientProxyOreSpawn.java:446 - the port's WINGSPEED): while the walking speed is above a thousandth the gait is the cosine of the age in ticks times 0.75 times the wingspeed, times pi, times the length of the entity's own movement since the last tick, times 0.4, clamped to 0.75 past 0.5 and -0.75 past -0.5 (0 on a probe that does not move), else 0. While the activity is not 0 the eight leg parts take a constant 1.0: the three right leg pieces pitch -0.58, 0.98 and -0.52 plus it and the right foot by it, the left the same; else the right side pitches the same rests plus the gait and the left side minus it. The ten wing parts roll by the cosine of the age times 0.55 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.28 while the activity is not 0, else -0.85 plus the cosine of the age times 0.2 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.028 at rest or -0.65 plus the cosine of the age times 0.9 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.068 attacking - the five left parts positive, the five right negative. The four top fins and four membranes pitch -1.85, -0.26, -2.07, -0.52, -2.42, -0.89, -2.63 and -1.11 minus the absolute value of the cosine of the age times 0.15 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.05, halved for each pair down the row. The tail speed is 0.76 and the amplitude 0.1, or 0.22 and 0.03 while the activity and the attacking flag are both 0: the first tail part yaws by the cosine of the age times the tail speed times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.04, the second and third by that cosine lagged 0.7853982 and twice that, times pi, times the amplitude, each placed 13 units from the part before along the cosine (z) and sine (x) of its yaw with 1.5 and -0.5 added to x; the four tail fins and three tail membranes yaw by the cosine lagged three times and sit 10 units on with -1.0 in x. While the activity is 1 the head yaw is the entity's own yaw delta times -10 eased into the per-entity render scratch by a fiftieth and clamped to plus or minus 50, else half the look yaw: the three necks yaw by it in radians times 0.125, 0.25 and 0.5 and the head, the two hammerheads and the mouth by 0.75, each neck placed 14 units back from the previous along its yaw with 0.5 added to x, the head 8 units on. The mouth pitches -0.61 plus the cosine of the age times 0.5 times the wingspeed, times pi, times 0.14 while attacking, else -0.87. The walk position and the look pitch play no part. The GeckoLib hook is the same (CephadromeGeoReplacement.applyCustomAnimations).
